A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HadamardNet research and contain complete, readable main text and supplements. Textual and visual inspection supports matching the equations, figures, tables and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original semantic segmentation, object detection and perturbation-detection experiments, including benchmark comparisons, loss ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a Cityscapes comparison of inconsistency-based detection with one-hot and Hadamard outputs.

M1.justification: HadamardNet, simplex decoding and the three anomaly scores remain unchanged. v1 Section 5 and Supplement J already select the MSE-only encoded-space loss; v2 foregrounds this choice in Section 3.4 and relocates the general loss formulation to Supplement H. The new one-hot variant serves as an experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Cityscapes, BDD100K and ADE20K segmentation, VOC, BDD100K and COCO object detection, and the same attacks and disturbances. The new control uses existing Cityscapes coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 adds one-hot+(17), a sigmoid-output one-hot model evaluated with simplex projection and the error-vector detector, against the entropy and Hadamard alternatives. Existing baseline comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new DeepLabv3+ experiment introduces a control that replaces softmax with sigmoid for one-hot outputs and applies the same projection and error score, while explicitly retaining the remaining setup. Existing splits, training budgets, attack settings and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Table 3 adds an ablation separating the contribution of prediction inconsistency from Hadamard encoding. Existing loss-function and classification-weight ablations, perturbation-strength analyses and ROC comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 95% confidence intervals over three seeds. The new comparison follows the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no changed run counts or statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: v2 Table 3 adds 76.9 ± 0.3% global AuROC for one-hot+(17). Its entropy and Hadamard comparison values, 72.5 ± 0.1% and 80.4 ± 1.1%, already appear in v1 Table 2. Existing benchmark and appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: The probabilistic formulation, error-minimization equivalence proof and simplex-projection derivation remain unchanged, including Supplements A–E. Relocated loss equations and the explicit statement of the previously selected loss do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: probabilistic Hadamard decoding, inconsistency-based perturbation detection and application to segmentation and object detection. The new experiment supports these claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 Section 5 newly interprets the control as showing benefits from both permitting prediction inconsistencies and using Hadamard encoding. Existing discussions of difficult disturbances, large-vocabulary datasets and unstable quantile detection for object detection are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability statement and repository URL in the abstract. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and implementation details remain in the renumbered supplements. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's contents or functionality.

R1.justification: The cited research and substantive positioning remain unchanged. v2 removes a duplicate SegFormer reference while retaining the same work, renumbers subsequent citations and edits bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Section 3.4 is shortened to emphasize the selected training objective, with the general loss discussion moved to a new Supplement H. v2 adds the control-experiment discussion and makes limited cross-reference and bibliography edits; the broader narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the compact comparison Table 3 and moves the training schematic from main-text Figure 2 to supplementary Figure 6. Existing displays are retained with modest sizing, spacing, placement and numbering adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new Table 3 provides a more informative control for attributing detection gains to Hadamard encoding, strengthening the evidence in the tested Cityscapes/DeepLabv3+ setting. Clearer presentation of the selected loss and the code-access pointer also help. These are limited improvements; the broader methods, experimental findings and limitations remain unchanged.
